security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or a JavaScript template literal. Three commands present real destructive-operation concerns: recursive temporary-directory deletion and forceful process termination. The guide also presents several destructive recovery actions without confirmation or data-loss warnings.

remediation.issue: Destructive recovery commands can delete development state or device data.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation step, describe the data-loss impact, and provide a less destructive diagnostic option before each cleanup or erase command.

remediation.issue: The port cleanup command forcefully kills a process without verifying ownership.
remediation.suggestion: First show the process name and PID, then ask the user to confirm. Prefer a normal termination before using kill -9.

remediation.issue: Wildcard deletion in /tmp can remove active tool state.
remediation.suggestion: List matching paths first and delete only tool-owned cache directories after user confirmation.

content.value_statement: React Native issues can span Metro, native builds, devices, and application code. This skill provides structured debugging steps and commands for isolating common problems.
actual_capabilities: Provides cache and dependency recovery steps for Metro bundler problems.
Guides investigation of iOS pods, Android Gradle builds, and Expo prebuild issues.
Lists commands for viewing iOS, Android, Metro, and ADB logs.
Shows a development-only React Native network inspector example.
Provides a render-time hook example for identifying slow React components.
Supplies a repeatable checklist for crashes, builds, and dependency errors.
limitations: It is a static troubleshooting guide and does not inspect an app automatically.
Some commands can remove caches, dependencies, simulator data, or running processes.
It does not diagnose production telemetry, backend services, or proprietary native SDKs.
Platform commands require the relevant React Native, Expo, Android, or iOS tools to be installed.

use_cases.title: Recover a blocked local build
use_cases.description: Use targeted cache, dependency, pod, and Gradle checks when a local React Native build fails.

use_cases.title: Investigate a device-only crash
use_cases.description: Collect Metro, Android, or iOS logs and compare the failure across supported platforms.

use_cases.title: Find a rendering slowdown
use_cases.description: Add the supplied render-time instrumentation and identify components that exceed a frame budget.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a Metro error
prompt_templates.prompt: My React Native app shows a Metro bundler error. Ask for the exact error, then give the safest checks in order.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an Android build failure
prompt_templates.prompt: My Android React Native build failed after a dependency update. Help me inspect versions, Gradle output, and native module compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a device crash
prompt_templates.prompt: My Expo app crashes on Android but not iOS. Create a step-by-step log collection and comparison plan before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Profile slow rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add development-only render timing to this React Native screen. Explain how to identify the slow component and avoid measuring production builds.

output_examples.input: Metro cannot resolve a module after I renamed a file.
output: Confirm the import path and filename casing.
Check recent changes and dependency state.
Clear the Metro cache only after reviewing the affected project.

output_examples.input: The Android app crashes only on a physical device.
output: Collect Android device logs while reproducing the crash.
Record the exception and the affected screen.
Compare package and native module versions with the working platform.

output_examples.input: A screen feels slow when scrolling.
output: Add render-time logging in development builds.
Identify components exceeding the frame budget.
Check subscriptions, timers, and cleanup functions.

best_practices: Reproduce the issue and preserve the full error before clearing caches or resetting tools.
Start with the least destructive check and confirm scope before deleting data or stopping processes.
Test each fix on the affected platform and record the result before changing another variable.
anti_patterns: Do not erase simulators or delete dependencies before collecting logs and confirming the issue.
Do not use forceful process termination without checking the process owner and port.
Do not assume an Android failure has the same cause as an iOS failure.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React Native and Expo troubleshooting workflows.

faq.question: Can it fix errors automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic steps, examples, and commands for guided investigation.

faq.question: Does it support both iOS and Android?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes platform-specific build, log, simulator, and device checks.

faq.question: Are the cleanup commands safe?
faq.answer: Some commands delete caches, dependencies, simulator data, or processes. Review the impact and confirm scope first.

faq.question: Can it help with performance issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes render-time instrumentation and cleanup guidance for common performance problems.

faq.question: Does it require Expo?
faq.answer: No. The guide includes React Native commands and additional Expo-specific troubleshooting steps.
